title: Normalized completed comparison for one refinement on qcqs schemes
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, a field k in which ell is invertible, finite-type k-schemes X and Y, and a separated finite-type k-morphism f:X→Y. Use the completed coefficient derived categories and integral constructible category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed; def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let c,d be compactifications of f and r:c→d a proper refinement [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For any integral constructible input K on X there exists an isomorphism rho from image(completed E,c)(K) to image(completed E,d)(K), satisfying SfCompletedRefinementSpec of [def-zl-field-shriek-composition-normalization]. Thus rho is the inverse proper compositor followed by d.g-pushforward of the inverse of the open-adjunction-normalized proper/open isomorphism. No separatedness of X or Y over k is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0F7B and 0F7J, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open and lemma-shriek-composition; completed-coefficient passage: Bhatt--Scholze Definition 6.7.6, Lemma 6.7.7 and Lemma 6.1.13.

proof.text: Use finiteRing_constructibleDerived_origin to retain a bounded-below etale origin for each bounded constructible finite-coefficient input. The finite_ring_refinement_coordinates_canonical theorem supplies its proper/open isomorphism and the actual open-unit normalization. The invertibility of refinementRestriction and injectivity of the open adjunction identify its hom with the already constructed refinementOpenMap; hence that particular finite map is invertible. This needs no finite-field datum or separated structure maps.

Let q be the compactification of d.i with open c.i and proper map r.hom. Its schemes inherit finite-type structure over the original field, and d.i is quasi-compact because f is. Apply refinementOpenMap_scalar to the canonical completed map and the positive quotient change. Its left side is reduction of the completed map followed by comparison(reduction,q); its right side is openComparison followed by the invertible finite map from step 1. The qcqs finite-comparison theorem makes comparison(reduction,q) invertible. Cancel it, then transport along finiteReductionIso to show every actual derived reduction of the completed map is invertible. Isomorphism closure of finite constructibility transfers the input condition along finiteReductionIso.

The source open extension is complete by the qcqs open-completeness theorem. The qcqs realization for q identifies the target proper/open object with its recorded integral constructible value, so the target is constructible. Reuse constructible_of_complete_reduction_isos from the normalized-isomorphism-existence module to obtain constructibility of the source from completeness and step 2. Reuse constructible_isIso_of_reductions there: the cone is integral constructible and complete, each reduction is zero, and its Roos triangle makes the cone zero. Thus the canonical completed refinementOpenMap is invertible. This argument detects invertibility and does not infer equality of maps from finite reductions or assume finite shifted Hom.

Take epsilon to be asIso of the canonical completed map. Define rho explicitly as inverse canonical proper composition along r.hom and d.g, transported by r.hom_g, followed by d.g-pushforward of epsilon inverse. refinementOpenMap_normalization supplies the first conjunct of SfCompletedRefinementSpec; the second is reflexivity of the constructed composite. Empty schemes and zero inputs require no separate nonemptiness hypotheses.

from.place: Proper/open normalization for refinement factors in the integral component proof. This supplies the compact-support composition used in the Leray spectral sequence of det-l-dl-general-composition.

lean.statement:
theorem sfQcqsCompletedRefinement_exists
    {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X) :
    ∃ ρ : (image (completed l E) c).obj K.obj ≅
        (image (completed l E) d).obj K.obj,
      SfCompletedRefinementSpec l E r K.obj ρ
